recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Further work on broader Vital Signs applicability should be handled under the later FHIR-41426/FHIR-50194 issue family rather than duplicating or weakening the FHIR-19738 text.
issue_request: FHIR-19738 asked to revise the Vital Signs profile set description so other Observation profiles reporting vital-sign-like measurements would not be interpreted as having to satisfy every Vital Signs profile requirement. The Applied/Persuasive with Modification resolution for R6 said the LOINC concern had been addressed by R6 ballot revisions and required revised Vital Signs introduction text plus an exception for measurements coming directly from a device before patient association.
initial_application: The Jira-tagged commit b01f2f50d238c69e12fd88a09deb1b349c925430, referenced from PR #3764 in Jira comments, updated source/observation/observation-vitalsigns-profile-introduction.xml with the resolved introduction and device exception. Follow-up commit 4632614fb92b6d7302a87d2cf9e9f028a0e47ea9 added de-identified data to the same exception.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists observation=Observation under active resources, making the Observation source folder build scope. Later Applied issue FHIR-41426 and commit 6cb98831954b3c61ed330358aaf541a79d0334d0 clarified the same Vital Signs introduction with value-set applicability guidance while preserving the FHIR-19738 exception. OO minutes from 2025-10-10 record the FHIR-19738 vote and the same device/gateway sentence; bounded Jira/Zulip/Confluence searches found no conflicting evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already states the global-vocabulary rationale, the SHALL conformance rule for listed vital signs, value-set applicability detail, and that de-identified data or direct device measurements not yet associated with a patient are not required to conform to the Vital Signs profiles.
